Class GraphPlaceFusion

java.lang.Object
ua.stetsenkoinna.graphnet.GraphPlaceFusion
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class GraphPlaceFusion extends Object implements Serializable
Two places of different Petri-objects drawn, and simulated, as one place.

A shared place is the classic way two Petri-objects are composed, and it is not an arc: nothing flows along it, the two places simply are the same place.

Always shown as a line (drawBetweenPorts(java.awt.Graphics2D, java.awt.Point, java.awt.Point, boolean)), one end anchored to whichever port stands for a framed half, the other to a free half's own position, and never moving either place. There used to be a second form for two free places, which stacked one on top of the other and drew a ring round the pair. It was unreachable while two free places could not be linked at all, and once they could it would have been wrong: a source repeated by several places would have piled all of them onto one point, destroying the layout and showing a ring that says nothing about what the place is linked to.

Which of the two is the master decides nothing about the semantics; it only fixes which object keeps the place instance when the model is built, and, for a free-place fusion, which one the other is moved onto.

  • Method Details

    • syncMarking

      public void syncMarking()
      Mirrors the master's marking onto the joined half. A shared place is one place with one marking - a PNML reference place carries no marking of its own, and the built simulation replaces the joined half's instance with the master's outright - but the editor used to keep showing each half's own token count, so the drawing displayed two different numbers for what the model runs as one.

    • drawBetweenPorts

      public void drawBetweenPorts(Graphics2D g2, Point masterPoint, Point joinedPoint, boolean selected)
      Draws a fusion anchored to at least one frame as a line between the two halves' drawn positions, a framed half's port or a free half's own position, since a locked place cannot be moved to sit on top of the other half the way two free places can.

      The line is a double line with an open arrowhead at the joined end, pointing from the master to the joined half: the joined place's marking is a consequence of what happens in the master, which is the assignment joined := master the simulation makes. It used to be dash-dot, which was still too easy to mistake for a dashed informational arc; a double line is a difference of kind from every arc on the canvas.

      Parameters:
      g2 - canvas graphics
      masterPoint - where the master half is drawn: its port if framed, its own position if free
      joinedPoint - the same for the joined half
      selected - whether the fusion is the current selection or lit by the animation
